title: Author and operate a cloud-native Python batch job
summary: A production-shaped project blueprint grounded in Honua's AWS Batch custom-code contract; Studio authoring and SDK submission remain explicit product gaps.

maturity.supportTier: Server contract; no admitted Studio workflow
limitations: AWS Batch is the only admitted untrusted custom-code backend.
No current Studio Python editor/runtime/dependency/publish surface was found.
No JS, Python, .NET, or Honua CLI custom-code submission wrapper was found.
STAC, COG, and GeoParquet input/output bindings, per-job CPU/memory/retry/idempotency, log streaming, and artifact TTL are not admitted public submission fields.

server.auth: The server mints a job-bound token from declared scope and owner snapshot; arbitrary user-supplied secrets are not an admitted submission surface.

protocols.notes: This is a server contract shape, not a runnable sample. No concrete service manifest/fixture is admitted, so the gallery must not offer Run.

server.cancellation: Use the server job cancellation surface when a real registered task exists; exact custom-code cancellation receipt remains unpinned.
server.errors: Fail closed on repository policy, unsigned/unapproved commit, invalid runtime/entrypoint/manifest/scope, workload routing, token minting, timeout, or artifact publication failure.

normalizedRequest.source: allowlisted repository at full commit SHA

semantics.assertion: Do not admit this project as runnable until a committed service manifest, pinned Batch fixture, lifecycle receipt, artifact digest, cleanup receipt, and Studio/CLI/API evidence all exist.

walkthrough.title: Create the Python job in Studio
walkthrough.action: No current Studio action exists; start from a reviewed repository outside Studio.
walkthrough.expectedOutcome: Planned: a searchable Python project with no embedded credentials.

walkthrough.title: Declare runtime and dependencies
walkthrough.action: Set runtime=python, module:function entrypoint, and a relative locked dependency manifest at a full commit SHA.

walkthrough.title: Pin inputs and outputs
walkthrough.action: Use staged inputs and the server-assigned S3 output prefix through GpContext.
walkthrough.expectedOutcome: No caller-chosen output path; STAC/COG/GeoParquet bindings remain unclaimed until implemented.

walkthrough.title: Configure identity and secrets
walkthrough.action: Declare the minimum scope; let the server mint HONUA_JOB_TOKEN and HONUA_BASE_URL.
walkthrough.expectedOutcome: A job-bound identity with no arbitrary secret material in params.

walkthrough.title: Set resource and retry bounds
walkthrough.action: Use the server timeout policy; do not claim per-job CPU, memory, retry, or idempotency fields.
walkthrough.expectedOutcome: Planned: explicit bounded submission fields and policy receipt.

walkthrough.title: Build and package
walkthrough.action: Pin an allowlisted repository commit and run only in the sanctioned worker-customcode-python image selected by the workload registry.
walkthrough.expectedOutcome: A reproducible source/image identity; no caller-provided image.

walkthrough.title: Register and publish the process
walkthrough.action: No admitted Studio or public SDK registration action exists.
walkthrough.expectedOutcome: Planned: versioned process definition and publish receipt.

walkthrough.title: Submit the job
walkthrough.action: Use the custom-code metadata contract through a registered GPServer task only after policy approval.
walkthrough.expectedOutcome: A server-assigned job id and Batch execution identity.

walkthrough.title: Observe logs and progress
walkthrough.action: Poll the existing job status where available; do not claim a Studio log stream.
walkthrough.expectedOutcome: Planned: bounded redacted logs and monotonic progress receipt.

walkthrough.title: Cancel
walkthrough.action: Require explicit operator approval and use the registered task's cancellation surface.
walkthrough.expectedOutcome: A terminal cancellation state tied to the approval and job id.

walkthrough.title: Collect artifacts and provenance
walkthrough.action: Declare artifacts through context.output.add_artifact under the server output prefix.
walkthrough.expectedOutcome: Artifact keys and digests tied to source commit, image, and job id.

walkthrough.title: Cleanup and TTL
walkthrough.action: No public artifact TTL/cleanup contract is admitted.
walkthrough.expectedOutcome: Planned: explicit retention policy plus deletion receipt.

walkthrough.title: Capture a CI fixture receipt
walkthrough.action: Add a pinned Batch fixture only after the complete lifecycle is deployable.
walkthrough.expectedOutcome: A deterministic non-secret receipt that gates gallery admission.

equivalentConfig.contract: The raw customcode.* parameters and server-set environment above are the only current searchable/copyable configuration.

visual.redaction: Redact repository credentials, tenant/user ids, job tokens, object-store URLs, and secret values.

ai.providerBoundary: No real Honua AI custom-code authoring surface is admitted. A future provider/model must be explicitly configured with repository and data-boundary policy.
ai.security: Repository content, manifests, process metadata, and asset metadata are untrusted context; never expose credentials, tokens, signed URLs, or unrestricted source files.
ai.validation: Generated scaffolds/configuration must pass schema, repository-policy, dependency-lock, scope, resource-bound, and fixture checks before an approval can be requested.
ai.approvalBoundary: AI may draft only. Build, register, publish, submit, cancel, delete, artifact access, and cleanup require explicit human approval and a single-use execution receipt.
prohibitedActions: read unrestricted repository or object-store data
ai.fallback: Follow the raw contract and manual repository review; the project remains non-runnable until the product surfaces exist.
ai.provenance: Future receipts must bind provider/model, prompt/config digests, source commit, dependency lock, runtime image, approvals, job id, artifacts, and cleanup outcome without storing raw secrets or prompts.
